en.title: Numbers with Distinct Decimal Digits in a Closed Range
en.description:
Count the non-negative integers in a closed range whose decimal digits are all different. 0 is written as the single digit 0 and counts as valid. The original statement is truncated; the rule is restored from the title and the original explanation that 10..13 includes 10, 12, and 13. The non-negative domain and the representation of 0 are an explicit protocol of this site.

The input/output protocol was compiled by this site, and missing numeric bounds are explicitly marked as site additions.
en.input: One line with start end. The original has no numeric bounds; this site uses 0≤start≤end≤10^18.
en.explanation: The outputs of the three public examples are, in order: 3; 11; 2. These answers have been checked by independent enumeration or direct simulation.
hints: Use digit DP to count the valid numbers not exceeding a bound, then compute F(end)−F(start−1). The state is the position, the mask of used digits, whether the number has started, and whether it is tight against the bound; leading zeros do not use up a digit.
